reviews.reason: The transverse Hilbert subspace, inherited second-variable pairing and bosonic representation remain the same. Countable Choice is explicit and the revised Weyl supplier defines the same local algebra with a bounded multiplication projection; no field or Born interpretation is broadened.

The framework change defines the autonomous spectral exponential, while this postulate uses only the unchanged flat chart, Clifford, units and charge conventions. Its local classical Dirac/Maxwell premise does not invoke an unconstructed interacting Hamiltonian.

The background scope now permits stating the dimension of the length action while leaving its motion law to this postulate. This carrier already supplies finite-segment C2 fixed-endpoint stationarity explicitly and uses the unchanged proper-time density.

The nonzero null covector gives a nonzero vertical differential of C0, so the used constraint surface is regular on its selected branch. The regular-constraint supplier empty-case and time-generator refinements do not invalidate this independently specified positive-einbein action.

The momentum supplier now writes the normalization for arbitrary C2 timelike curves explicitly. This postulate already chooses proper time, g(U,U)=-c2, constant positive mass and a smooth orthogonal bundle force, so D_tau P=f and the local shell IVP retain their precise domain.

The collision supplier adds explicit SI units f=s3/m6, Q=f/s and measure units m9/s7; these match this postulate's density and collision equation. This carrier independently adopts a measurable locally integrable representative and its weak identity, including a nonnegative branch, without claiming the positive-only mathematical theorem for every solution.

The field supplier now makes divergence conditional on existence of spatial partials. Fourier's pointwise flux and quadratic form here require only the already supplied temperature gradient. Its additional entropy interpretation explicitly requires the energy balance and product/chain-rule regularity; no differentiation of arbitrary optional flux is assumed.

The conditional divergence in the revised field definition is fully licensed here: j_Q and all first spatial partial derivatives must extend continuously on every compact time slab. Its boundary trace and classical balance remain well defined with the original insulation and no-source premises.

This carrier uses the supplied positive C1 caloric u and continuous c=u' on the positive temperature interval. The entropy integral and c/T derivative do not differentiate optional flux or K, so the supplier's conditional-divergence clarification changes no adopted entropy relation.

The enlarged process transfer-map domain and exact core energy-balance class do not affect the separately declared cooling operations and boundary reachability exclusion. Positive-temperature portions retain process conventions; no core-only first-law balance is invoked for arbitrary cooling records.

The contact supplier now defines the tagged-family relation by selected equilibrium records, unchanged constituent endpoints and the exact zero internal-transfer predicate. This postulate explicitly adopts reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity on that very relation, rather than inferring them from the definition; the refined protocol-relative relation is compatible.

Verified the conserved radial polynomial, positive C branch and continuation against the unchanged Coulomb ODE. The prior outside counterexample is correct: at J=kappa/c, Q=A-2du still has a positive admissible simple root. Corrected only Proof 7.1's necessity overstatement; the full Statement, exact angle and physical_scope are unchanged.

The revised covariance supplier proves ker K_D=C Omega, not literal vector uniqueness. Corrected the Statement, F4 and final proof to that exact eigenspace and normalized phase convention. Positive hbar c scaling preserves the domain and kernel, gap and forward spectrum. The existing CAR/locality/covariance deductions are unaffected by this scalar-multiple correction.

The scaling supplier adds E(t) and E_delta(t) as explicit sets without altering dilation or scaling degree. This proof already constructs T_mu, derives its logarithmic delta difference, proves degree four and invokes the same-degree affine classification. The added notation licenses the existing family language without changing the anomaly coefficient.

Its framework use is the unchanged Minkowski, length, Clifford and field-dimension dictionary. Classical action variations are explicitly compactly supported; scalar and Dirac weak test equations follow from their constructed smearing maps. No autonomous exponential is invoked, so the new spectral definition adds no unmet hypothesis here.

This theorem uses only the unchanged SI/natural conversion and fixed finite Clifford matrices. The magnetic H_D is explicitly a differential expression on C_c^infinity, with no self-adjoint closure or autonomous evolution asserted. Therefore the new spectral-calculus clause does not demand an unavailable magnetic operator construction.

H0 is an everywhere-defined Hermitian finite matrix, so its exponential satisfies the revised dense self-adjoint spectral convention under the explicit Countable Choice premise. The time-dependent unitary is separately constructed by the finite Dyson theorem. Its Hermitian imaginary part is already defined explicitly, and the Kraus normalization and truncation bounds retain their exact model scope.

The Fock definition now limits its closed-domain cross-reference to separable H. This theorem proves transverse-Hilbert separability in step 1.2 before using Segal-Weyl in step 4.1; its contractions and tensor norms are unchanged. The explicit cutoff coherent vector remains in the energy domain, and its adjacent-shell ray-distance proof uses those same sector norms.

The revised Fock domain cross-reference applies here because F8 identifies the actual transverse space as separable by the supplier's projected countable dense set. Countable Choice is explicit; each P_n is used in a normalized finite two-outcome instrument. The framework use is only the unchanged energy-coordinate conversion, not an arbitrary autonomous Hamiltonian.

The revised Weyl supplier makes its L2 multiplication projection and Hilbert range explicit without changing g_h, sqrt(2) normalization, local algebras or separation condition. This proof uses exactly those maps for real compact antisymmetric tests and chooses open spacelike neighborhoods of their compact supports, so field and bounded-algebra locality remain licensed.

The framework change adds a spectral construction compatible with the explicit self-adjoint maximal sector multiplier already assumed here. Positive hbar c scaling preserves its domain and positivity. The transverse rank-two fibers, global Hilbert quotient and Lorentz action do not use any changed evolution convention or literal vacuum-vector uniqueness claim.

The current-conservation supplier now requires that polarization-shift momentum match the current's own transfer up to sign. This theorem explicitly sets k=p-p'=q'-q; step 1.2 proves k dot J1=k dot J2=0 before the longitudinal and polarization contractions. Thus both current uses meet the refined hypothesis, while the separate finite formal-matrix identities are unchanged.

The scalar-model Definition repairs the classical action to compact variation differences. This consumer uses only its unchanged one-particle shell, finite-particle field, vacuum and Weyl representation, not a global classical action integral. The ordered moment recursion, bounded Weyl expectation and distributional time-kernel normalization retain their exact prerequisites.

The only changed supplier here is the framework's autonomous spectral convention. F8 and the current Statement use its unchanged length-coordinate, spinor-dimension and SI charge conversion clauses to derive a smooth compact-variation Maxwell-Dirac PDE. No quantum Hamiltonian exponential or Hilbert operator is used by that deduction.

F7-F8 use the unchanged x0=ct, positive SI constants and spinor engineering dimension. Its classical finite-mode Legendre constraints and periodic Fourier Poisson solution invoke no autonomous quantum evolution. The added spectral clause therefore changes neither the classical scalar source nor the neutral-branch and finite-mode qualifications.

The time-ordering supplier now explicitly fixes X=R4 and zero-variable kernels. This remark already works on R4 and proves the quartic second-derivative kernel is nonzero diagonal-supported, hence not smooth regular. Its exclusion from the regular contraction domain remains exact, and no extension across the diagonal is inferred.

The framework's only used clause assigns inverse-length units to the bump's momentum scale. The normalized negative auxiliary packet is explicitly outside K0, while the transverse projected packet has positive norm at least 8/9 before normalization. No evolution or probability is assigned to the auxiliary vector, so the new spectral construction is irrelevant to the inference.

The Fock definition's revised relation scope changes no sector formula used here: finite-cutoff tensor powers and their square-summable coherent vector are explicit. Number/energy domains are checked through the Poisson second moment and actual maximal multipliers. Countable Choice and inverse-length cutoffs are stated; the corrected spectral convention matches the supplied self-adjoint free energy.

The affected uses are F6/F15/F18/F19 and proof 1.2: sector creation/contraction formulas, product pairing, finite support and orthogonal symmetrization. These clauses are unchanged by limiting the separate closed-domain cross-reference to separable H. The proof derives its finite-sector bound directly and never applies a generic-H closed-domain CCR claim.

The revised time-ordering Definition supplies the formerly implicit X=R4 with unchanged relative lift and independent-variable contraction formulas. This theorem uses exactly R4, compact regular polynomial inputs and the empty-block T0=1 branch. Its coefficientwise binomial factorization and support replacement remain valid with no local Wick-product extension claimed.
